what: Every mode the plugin plays, with what is actually known about how wide its line is at room temperature, as a bracket (narrowest and widest plausible width, cm^-1). Q = line / width; a narrow line is a long ring. Built 2026-11-14, steward cycle 15, for the plan's move 'give every mode its own ring'.

kinds.raman_measured: a Raman line whose room-temperature width I found a source for, this cycle or cycle 12
kinds.raman_range: a Raman line where I found only a range for the mineral's lines (or its family), not this line
kinds.raman_unread: a Raman line whose width exists in the literature but I could not read it this cycle (rate-limited or paywalled)
kinds.not_raman: not a Raman line at all: a zone-boundary or infrared phonon, or an approximate pick from a dense spectrum. No Raman width exists to look up. Bracketed by the rule: half to double the crystal's anchor Q range.

crystals.name: Diamond
crystals.anchor_note: first-order Raman line, 1.65 +/- 0.02 (Prawer & Nemanich 2004); other sources 1.0-1.5

crystals.name: Fluorite
crystals.anchor_note: T2g 322: 12 for a powder standard (Caries Res. 27:445); a clear single crystal is likely narrower, 5 is my guess at the floor

crystals.name: Emerald
crystals.anchor_note: beryl/emerald ring line near 686: FWHM 9-12 across localities, Colombian lowest (Raman microspectroscopy of emeralds from various deposits)

crystals.name: Ruby
crystals.anchor_note: corundum A1g 418; the room-temperature width is in Appl. Opt. 56, 8598 (2017) but OSTI refused the PDF this cycle (HTTP 429). 2.5-6 is my bracket for a clean oxide single crystal, not a reading

crystals.name: Amethyst
crystals.anchor_note: alpha-quartz 464: 7-8 at 300 K (Schmidt & Ziemann, Am. Mineral. 85:1725, via summaries); a second summary gives about 8

modes.label: cage (E)
modes.note: Pine & Tannenwald, Phys. Rev. 178:1424 (1969) measured it 5-300 K; ADS refused the abstract

modes.label: soft mode
modes.note: known broad and fast-broadening; no number read

crystals.name: Topaz
crystals.anchor_note: topaz: 'bands below 700 cm-1 are sharp, typical FWHM 2-10; above 800 broader, up to 30' (Am. Mineral. 111:1046, fluorine in topaz, via summary)

crystals.name: Labradorite
crystals.anchor_note: plagioclase's strongest line 506-508: FWHM 7-20 in crystalline plagioclase; albite 7.9, anorthite 10.7 (shock study, Mistastin Lake; Freeman et al. Can. Mineral. 46:1477)
